definitions.statement: An Engineering Role Profile is a versioned description of one engineering role and level, its actual tasks, critical incidents, required capabilities, working conditions and success criteria, selected before assessment design.
definitions.scope: One employer or declared role family and level.
boundaries: A job title alone is not a Role Profile.
A profile does not prove a case predicts success.

definitions.statement: A Target Outcome is a predeclared, independently observed performance criterion for role R in population P at horizon T and hiring capacity C, with raters, components and missing-data rules fixed before assessment scores are analyzed.
definitions.scope: One named validation study and role context.
boundaries: The assessment score or hiring decision cannot serve as its own outcome.
One employer's outcome is not a universal best-engineer definition.

parameters.name: C
parameters.interpretation: Positive count of candidates selected under the policy; selection fraction is derived from the declared pool size.

definitions.statement: An Assessment Construct is a named capability or behavior the assessment intends to infer, with observable indicators, rival explanations, role linkage and a declared interpretation limit.
boundaries: A construct name does not prove it can be measured.
Creativity, analysis and ingenuity remain distinct hypotheses until evidence supports their structure.

definitions.statement: A Case Family is a controlled set of prompts sharing an intended reasoning operation and scoring blueprint while varying surface content, constraints and exposure history.
definitions.scope: Question generation, comparison and item-bank governance.
boundaries: Family membership does not establish equal difficulty.
A familiar riddle and an unreleased variant may have different exposure effects.

definitions.statement: A Case Version is an immutable administered prompt sequence with source, family, allowed information reveals, timing, media, accessibility alternatives, scoring blueprint and exposure state pinned by content identity.
boundaries: Editing a prompt creates a new version.
Novel wording does not establish quality or equivalence.

definitions.statement: An Assessment Session is one participant's bounded encounter with one Case Version under a pinned administration policy, producing at most ten minutes of recorded answer and an attributable event history.
definitions.scope: One of at most three sessions in an assessment attempt.
boundaries: The session is not the candidate or the score.
Preparation time and accommodations require explicit policy rather than silent inference.

definitions.statement: A Candidate Response is the source recording and ordered answer events produced in an Assessment Session, with exact custody identity and participant correction history.
definitions.scope: One session response under one purpose and consent state.
boundaries: A response is an observation, not a trait or performance conclusion.
The recording does not grant research reuse or public release.

definitions.statement: A Transcript is a versioned text rendering of a Candidate Response with method, uncertainty markers and corrections linked to the immutable source recording.
boundaries: A transcript is not the response original.
Transcript confidence is not scoring confidence.

definitions.statement: A Rubric is a frozen set of construct-linked observable criteria, anchored performance levels, alternative-valid-answer rules and missing-evidence handling for specified Case Versions.
definitions.scope: One assessment purpose, role and compatible case set.
boundaries: A rubric is not evidence of validity.
A canonical punchline cannot be the sole creativity criterion.

definitions.statement: A Scoring Run is a reproducible application of one pinned Rubric and scorer configuration to one pinned response/transcript input, producing criterion ratings, cited evidence, uncertainty and errors.
definitions.scope: Human, model-assisted or model-generated rating under a declared method.
boundaries: A scoring receipt does not prove the score is valid.
A model may suggest ratings but cannot grant employment-use authority.

definitions.statement: A Score Report is a purpose-limited presentation of Scoring Run results, criterion evidence, uncertainty, missing observations, correction status and permitted interpretation.
definitions.scope: Participant feedback or separately governed employer use.
boundaries: A challenge report cannot silently become a hiring decision.
A percentile requires an identified comparison population and calibrated forms.

definitions.statement: A Validation Study is a preregistered, source-pinned comparison of assessment policies against independently specified outcomes, populations, costs and error analyses, with development and held-out evidence kept distinct.
definitions.scope: One claim, role and target-use context.
boundaries: Rater agreement alone is not predictive validity.
A voluntary challenge cohort alone cannot establish employer deployment validity.

definitions.statement: A Claim Tier is a bounded statement of what the current evidence permits the product owner to say or use, ordered from idea through reproducibility, reliability, prediction, accepted selection and observed value.
definitions.scope: Public, participant and employer communications for one product version.
boundaries: Higher tier is not inherited from a lower tier.
Changing role, language, model or population can invalidate an earlier tier.

definitions.statement: A Consent Record is an attributable purpose-specific participant choice and notice version governing capture, feedback, optional research reuse, sharing and withdrawal or deletion routes.
definitions.scope: One participant and declared processing purposes.
boundaries: Challenge participation does not imply research or model-training consent.
A consent record is not an employment-use validation decision.

definitions.statement: A Cohort is a defined set of participants selected by declared eligibility, recruitment, time window and sampling process for one research or validation purpose.
definitions.scope: One study and its analysis populations.
boundaries: Self-selected challengers are not automatically representative of applicants.
Cohort membership alone does not grant data access.

definitions.statement: A Decision Policy is a frozen mapping from specified score inputs and uncertainty to a selection action at a stated capacity, with abstention, human review, accommodation and appeal rules.
definitions.scope: One role, population, employer, jurisdiction and claim tier.
boundaries: A model score does not enact a hiring decision.
A policy is not effective until the employer and applicable owners authorize that exact use.
